ranked_facts.why: The presence of prior abdominal surgery supports adhesions as the underlying cause, as adhesions are a common complication of abdominal surgery, whereas norovirus gastroenteritis is less likely to be related to prior surgery.

The presence of a small bowel obstruction pattern supports adhesions as the underlying cause, as adhesions can cause mechanical obstruction of the small bowel, whereas norovirus gastroenteritis typically does not cause a mechanical obstruction pattern.
